input.title: Investor letter - wind-down (Feb 2026)
input.bodyText:
Subject: Harmony Games - winding down the company

Hi everyone,

I'm writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down Harmony Games. I wanted each of you to hear it from me first, and this letter sets out where things stand and what it means for you.

What happened
We reached this decision on February 9, 2026, after a thorough review of the most recent data across our products and the realistic set of options in front of us. Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
- We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybrid-casual gameplay with RPG depth: Domino Delights (domino/tripeaks solitaire with RPG elements), Zombie Match 3D (a Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat and progression) and Combo Fighter (Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements).
- We took real creative risks and explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution, including a bridge and recap in January, but none changed the trajectory enough. The latest Combo Fighter retention data confirmed we are not investable in our current form.
- We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025; revenue never reached meaningful levels and we ended January with roughly a month of runway.
- The team has stopped. Our remaining contractors' engagements ended on December 31, 2025 and January 31, 2026, and we told the full team on February 11 and sent everyone written termination letters the same day.

Where things stand
- Holders: as of today Carta shows 20 stockholders and optionholders besides the three founders: Griffin Gaming Partners (two funds), eleven angel investors and eight former team members whose options are still within their exercise window. Several former team members' options have already expired.
- Board: the board now consists of me and Robert. Griffin's board representative stepped down on February 12, and we thank him for his support over the last three years.
- Process: we have engaged Sunset, a specialist wind-down firm, to run an orderly dissolution. Their legal team is preparing the Plan of Dissolution and will handle the Delaware dissolution, our withdrawals from California and North Carolina, creditor communications and final tax and accounting close-out. Formal notices and any stockholder approvals will come to you separately from Sunset's legal team.
- Vendors: we have terminated or are closing out all vendor and service contracts, and we expect to cover the company's remaining obligations, including paying off our bank credit line, without leaving debts on anyone's books.

What it means for you
- Distributions: the company is insolvent. After obligations are settled we do not expect any cash to be available for distribution to stockholders, and the preferred stock's preferences do not change that. If anything is left once the dissolution is complete, it will be distributed according to our charter and you will hear from us.
- Tax papers: Sunset will prepare the company's final returns. Any documents you need for your own taxes (for example, to record the loss on your shares) will be sent to you once the dissolution is filed, and your Carta account stays available in the meantime.
- Options: former team members' options can still be exercised until the last day shown in Carta, but because the shares are expected to have no value, we do not recommend exercising. No action is needed; unexercised options simply lapse on their last day.

What happens to the games and the IP
- We are sunsetting the live games in a controlled way and moving player support off third-party tools.
- On February 12 we signed a data licensing agreement for anonymised game data. It brings in enough cash to cover the cost of an orderly wind-down, and the agreement confirms that the company keeps full ownership of its IP.
- We are still evaluating what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale or other disposition) and will keep you informed.

Thank you
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company. Thank you for backing us, for your advice and for your patience. I will send short updates as the major steps are completed and once the final position is clear.

If you would like to talk 1:1, reply here and I will make time.

Thank you,
Leonard Hayes
CEO and Co-founder, Harmony Games Inc.
leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co
